new_value: Closed as superseded/not normative in the current LICHEN EDHOC profile; no code changes required. spec/06-security.md §8.9 defines only the RFC 9528 three-message EDHOC exchange and explicitly requires periodic refresh by re-running EDHOC every 24 hours or at OSCORE sequence exhaustion. It defines no ticket, PSK binder, 0-RTT, abbreviated handshake, wire format, state machine, replay policy, or test oracle for "session resumption." Repository-wide searches of the Python EDHOC implementation, in-repo Rust wrapper, vectors, and the dirty external Rust oscore dependency found no resumption API/format. Durable OSCORE context continuity is separate: Python MemorySecurityContext.from_edhoc supports restoring a persisted sender sequence, and Rust Context::restore_existing restores authoritative sender state; that preserves nonce/replay safety after reboot but is not EDHOC session resumption. Key refresh is separately owned by 13.4.2. Adding an ad-hoc resumption protocol would violate interoperability and expand beyond RFC 9528/current spec. The stale Python/Rust/Zephyr/vector resumption beads 6.8.10-.13 should be reconciled separately rather than used as an implementation oracle.
